concept.title: The Four-Platform Tax Nobody Warned You About
concept.core_idea: A solo operator sits down on a Sunday afternoon to 'knock out social content for the week' across LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts — and a running on-screen tally of actual time spent reveals the real cost before they've posted a single thing.
concept.product_role: fenrik Studio is named at the resolution as the mechanism that eliminates the reformatting loop entirely — one URL input produces platform-ready assets for all four channels simultaneously. The product is not positioned as a shortcut; it's positioned as the removal of a tax the viewer didn't know they were paying.
concept.why_it_works: The fear hook is concrete and specific — not 'content is hard' but 'watch three hours disappear in real time.' The running timer mechanic is visual, native to short-form video, and makes an abstract pain point feel measurable and undeniable. The twist reframes the loss — it's not just one afternoon, it's every topic, every week. The resolution earns its place because the problem has been fully dramatized before the product appears. The witty friend voice keeps the tone light enough that the viewer smiles through the discomfort rather than scrolling past it.
concept.narrative_arc: SETUP: Drop mid-scene — a solo founder at a kitchen table, laptop open, coffee still hot, genuinely optimistic. Caption on screen: 'Sunday 2pm. Gonna smash out this week's content.' They open a blank doc and type 'LinkedIn post.' A small timer appears in the corner. CONFLICT: Cut through the next 90 seconds in rapid, slightly comedic time-lapse. LinkedIn: draft, redraft, reformat for professional tone — timer hits 45 minutes. Instagram: same message, now needs a hook caption, line breaks, five hashtags, a visual — timer hits 1 hr 20 min. TikTok: completely different format, needs a spoken hook, a trending angle, a script that sounds natural not written — timer hits 2 hrs 10 min. YouTube Shorts: vertical cut, different pacing, description copy, tags — timer hits 3 hrs 05 min. Each platform gets a small icon and a running total. The coffee is cold. The founder hasn't posted anything yet. TWIST: A second caption appears: 'That was just one topic. You have four weeks of content to fill.' The founder stares at the screen. Not panicked — just quietly doing the math. On-screen text: '3 hours. 1 topic. 0 posts published.' RESOLUTION: Calm voiceover: 'fenrik Studio takes your website URL and delivers ready-to-post videos, captions, and hashtags for all four platforms — no camera, no reformatting, no Sunday afternoon gone.' CTA slides in clean. PUNCHLINE ENERGY: The humor is in the tally — not mocking the founder, mocking the task itself.
concept.emotional_tone: Wry and relatable — the viewer recognizes themselves immediately and laughs before they feel the sting. The revelation is practical, not dramatic. The resolution feels like relief, not rescue.
concept.audience_insight: Solo operators and small teams genuinely underestimate the platform-switching tax. They budget for 'an hour of content' without accounting for the fact that LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts each have distinct formats, tones, and technical requirements. The real cost isn't writing — it's reformatting the same idea four times from scratch. Showing this as a running clock makes an invisible problem suddenly visible and quantifiable.

visual_direction.palette: Warm off-white and light oak tones for the environment; the timer and platform badges use clean, high-contrast white-on-dark chips so they read instantly on a phone screen at thumb-scroll speed.
visual_direction.lighting: Soft natural afternoon window light, slightly warm. As the time-lapse progresses and the afternoon fades, the light shifts subtly cooler and dimmer — a visual metaphor for the day slipping away without being heavy-handed about it.
visual_direction.environment: A lived-in kitchen table doubling as a workspace — laptop, a notebook, a coffee mug. Not a polished studio or a dark office. Feels like a real Sunday afternoon, not a stock photo. A window with soft daylight visible in the background.
visual_direction.camera_style: Mostly static medium shot on the founder at the table, with occasional tight cuts to the laptop screen showing the blank doc and the timer. Time-lapse sequences are slightly sped up with a subtle zoom drift to signal time passing. No shaky cam — clean and readable at mobile scale.
visual_direction.art_direction: Clean, slightly warm realism. The running timer in the corner is the hero graphic element — bold, simple, impossible to ignore. Each platform gets a small recognizable icon badge as it's introduced. On-screen text overlays are minimal and punchy — no decorative elements, just the numbers doing the work.
visual_direction.character_style: One solo founder — gender-neutral presentation, casual weekend clothes (plain sweatshirt, no branding), early 30s, looks competent not stressed. The character is the straight-man; the comedy comes from the situation, not from the person being foolish.

opening.pacing: Quick and engaging, setting up a comedic time-lapse that contrasts optimism with the reality of the task ahead.
opening.emotion: Wry and relatable, evoking a sense of shared frustration.

opening.attention_pattern: The timer's presence creates immediate curiosity about how long it will take to produce content, hinting at the hidden costs of managing multiple platforms.

package.title: The Four-Platform Tax Nobody Warned You About
package.hook: It's Sunday at 2pm, and you're ready to tackle this week's social content.
package.scenario: A solo SaaS founder clears their Sunday afternoon to produce one week of social content across LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts. They open a blank document at 2pm feeling genuinely optimistic. By 5pm they have four half-finished drafts in different tabs, a cold coffee, and zero published posts. The problem was never the idea — it was reformatting the same idea four times from scratch, for four platforms with completely different formats, tones, and technical requirements. The afternoon is gone. The content is not.

video.script:
SCENE 1 — SETUP
[Medium shot. Solo founder at kitchen table, laptop open, coffee steaming. Blank document on screen. Timer appears in corner: 0:00.]
VO: 'It's Sunday at 2pm, and you're ready to tackle this week's social content.'
On-screen text: 'Sunday 2pm. One topic. Four platforms. Let's go.'

SCENE 2 — CONFLICT: LINKEDIN
[Slight time-lapse. Founder typing, deleting, retyping. Timer: 0:45.]
VO: 'LinkedIn post — 45 minutes.'
On-screen badge: LinkedIn icon. Timer chip: 45 min.

SCENE 3 — CONFLICT: INSTAGRAM
[Cut to founder scrolling for a visual reference, rewriting caption with line breaks. Timer: 1:20.]
VO: 'Instagram caption plus visuals — another 35.'
On-screen badge: Instagram icon. Timer chip: 1 hr 20 min.

SCENE 4 — CONFLICT: TIKTOK + YOUTUBE
[Rapid time-lapse. Founder speaking quietly to themselves, scripting, scrapping, rewriting. Light through window shifts cooler. Timer: 2:10, then 3:05.]
VO: 'TikTok needs a completely different script — add 50 minutes. YouTube Shorts — different pacing, different copy — you're now at three hours.'
On-screen badges: TikTok icon, YouTube icon. Running total chip: 3 hrs 05 min.

SCENE 5 — TWIST
[Static shot. Founder stares at screen. Coffee mug untouched and cold. On-screen text appears: '3 hours. 1 topic. 0 posts published.']
VO: 'Coffee's cold. Nothing is posted. That was one topic.'

SCENE 6 — RESOLUTION
[Clean cut. Calm. Laptop screen shows fenrik Studio logo asset.]
VO: 'fenrik Studio turns your website URL into ready-to-post content for all four platforms — no reformatting required.'
CTA card slides in: 'Save this so you remember what Sunday actually costs you.'

linkedin.caption:
Most solo operators budget about an hour for 'content this week.' What they don't budget for is the platform-switching tax.

LinkedIn needs a professional tone and structured copy. Instagram needs a hook, line breaks, and hashtags. TikTok needs a spoken script that sounds unscripted. YouTube Shorts needs different pacing and separate metadata.

Same topic. Four complete rewrites. Three hours later — nothing published.

The cost isn't writing the idea. It's reformatting it four times from scratch, every single week.

If that math is quietly eating your Sundays, you're not alone.

video_concept.core_idea: A solo operator sits down on a Sunday afternoon to 'knock out social content for the week' across LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts — and a running on-screen tally of actual time spent reveals the real cost before they've posted a single thing.
video_concept.product_role: fenrik Studio is named at the resolution as the mechanism that eliminates the reformatting loop entirely — one URL input produces platform-ready assets for all four channels simultaneously. The product is not positioned as a shortcut; it's positioned as the removal of a tax the viewer didn't know they were paying.
video_concept.why_it_works: The fear hook is concrete and specific — not 'content is hard' but 'watch three hours disappear in real time.' The running timer mechanic is visual, native to short-form video, and makes an abstract pain point feel measurable and undeniable. The twist reframes the loss — it's not just one afternoon, it's every topic, every week. The resolution earns its place because the problem has been fully dramatized before the product appears. The witty friend voice keeps the tone light enough that the viewer smiles through the discomfort rather than scrolling past it.
video_concept.narrative_arc: SETUP: Drop mid-scene — a solo founder at a kitchen table, laptop open, coffee still hot, genuinely optimistic. Caption on screen: 'Sunday 2pm. Gonna smash out this week's content.' They open a blank doc and type 'LinkedIn post.' A small timer appears in the corner. CONFLICT: Cut through the next 90 seconds in rapid, slightly comedic time-lapse. LinkedIn: draft, redraft, reformat for professional tone — timer hits 45 minutes. Instagram: same message, now needs a hook caption, line breaks, five hashtags, a visual — timer hits 1 hr 20 min. TikTok: completely different format, needs a spoken hook, a trending angle, a script that sounds natural not written — timer hits 2 hrs 10 min. YouTube Shorts: vertical cut, different pacing, description copy, tags — timer hits 3 hrs 05 min. Each platform gets a small icon and a running total. The coffee is cold. The founder hasn't posted anything yet. TWIST: A second caption appears: 'That was just one topic. You have four weeks of content to fill.' The founder stares at the screen. Not panicked — just quietly doing the math. On-screen text: '3 hours. 1 topic. 0 posts published.' RESOLUTION: Calm voiceover: 'fenrik Studio takes your website URL and delivers ready-to-post videos, captions, and hashtags for all four platforms — no camera, no reformatting, no Sunday afternoon gone.' CTA slides in clean. PUNCHLINE ENERGY: The humor is in the tally — not mocking the founder, mocking the task itself.
video_concept.emotional_tone: Wry and relatable — the viewer recognizes themselves immediately and laughs before they feel the sting. The revelation is practical, not dramatic. The resolution feels like relief, not rescue.
video_concept.audience_insight: Solo operators and small teams genuinely underestimate the platform-switching tax. They budget for 'an hour of content' without accounting for the fact that LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts each have distinct formats, tones, and technical requirements. The real cost isn't writing — it's reformatting the same idea four times from scratch. Showing this as a running clock makes an invisible problem suddenly visible and quantifiable.

visual_direction.environment: A lived-in kitchen table doubling as a workspace — laptop, a notebook, a coffee mug. Not a polished studio or a dark office. Feels like a real Sunday afternoon, not a stock photo. A window with soft daylight visible in the background.
visual_direction.camera_style: Mostly static medium shot on the founder at the table, with occasional tight cuts to the laptop screen showing the blank doc and the timer. visual_direction.art_direction: Clean, slightly warm realism. The running timer in the corner is the hero graphic element — bold, simple, impossible to ignore. Each platform gets a small recognizable icon badge as it's introduced. On-screen text overlays are minimal and punchy — no decorative elements, just the numbers doing the work.
visual_direction.character_style: One solo founder — gender-neutral presentation, casual weekend clothes (plain sweatshirt, no branding), early 30s, looks competent not stressed. The character is the straight-man; the comedy comes from the situation, not from the person being foolish.

video.script:
SCENE 1 — SETUP
[Medium shot. Solo founder at kitchen table, laptop open, coffee steaming. Blank document on screen. Timer appears in corner: 0:00.]
VO: 'It's Sunday at 2pm, and you're ready to tackle this week's social content.'
On-screen text: 'Sunday 2pm. One topic. Four platforms. Let's go.'

SCENE 2 — CONFLICT: LINKEDIN
[Slight time-lapse. Founder typing, deleting, retyping. Timer: 0:45.]
VO: 'LinkedIn post — 45 minutes.'
On-screen badge: LinkedIn icon. Timer chip: 45 min.

SCENE 3 — CONFLICT: INSTAGRAM
[Cut to founder scrolling for a visual reference, rewriting caption with line breaks. Timer: 1:20.]
VO: 'Instagram caption plus visuals — another 35.'
On-screen badge: Instagram icon. Timer chip: 1 hr 20 min.

SCENE 4 — CONFLICT: TIKTOK + YOUTUBE
[Rapid time-lapse. Founder speaking quietly to themselves, scripting, scrapping, rewriting. Light through window shifts cooler. Timer: 2:10, then 3:05.]
VO: 'TikTok needs a completely different script — add 50 minutes. YouTube Shorts — different pacing, different copy — you're now at three hours.'
On-screen badges: TikTok icon, YouTube icon. Running total chip: 3 hrs 05 min.

SCENE 5 — TWIST
[Static shot. Founder stares at screen. Coffee mug untouched and cold. On-screen text appears: '3 hours. 1 topic. 0 posts published.']
VO: 'Coffee's cold. Nothing is posted. That was one topic.'

SCENE 6 — RESOLUTION
[Clean cut. Calm. Laptop screen shows fenrik Studio logo asset.]
VO: 'fenrik Studio turns your website URL into ready-to-post content for all four platforms — no reformatting required.'
CTA card slides in: 'Save this so you remember what Sunday actually costs you.'
